checks: Existing focused check: cargo test -p world --lib exec::tests -- --nocapture. Named tests: batches_preserve_order_and_cardinality (101 mapped values and empty input); worker_panics_are_errors_instead_of_partial_results (four panicking jobs). The file-root model.md#evidence records actual execution. Mode caching, exit behavior, mixed worker outcomes, GPU shape guards and GPU/CPU agreement remain untested here.
Six native exec tests: complete finite callback fibers, joined panic prefixes, output Drop accounting and stateful ticket projections; source-extracted compiled reverse-callback mutant.
cost: For n jobs, total work is sum of job costs plus O(n+t) aggregation; ideal span is largest chunk cost plus joins. GPU adds loading, model work and O(tokens) intermediate storage; no measured speedup.
description: Initialize mode once; CPU parses through ordered workers; GPU composes cached load, tokenize, nonempty gather, predict, shape guards, complete, repair, lowercase and scatter.
forward: Initialize mode once; CPU parses through ordered workers; GPU composes cached load, tokenize, nonempty gather, predict, shape guards, complete, repair, lowercase and scatter.
inverse: U consists of (build, environment history, texts, tagged Ok/Error/Exit outcome). R selects the latched mode and executes its pipeline. U minus R includes successful truncated returns after worker panic, successful GPU dispatch in a CPU-only build, and switching mode after a valid latch. Resource aborts and parser quality are outside this bound.
For Ok word batches y, R^-1(y) contains all texts and parser states mapping to y, with input count equal to output count. Casing, ambiguity and approximate GPU outputs prevent unique text recovery.
limitations: AST and semantic proof absent; parent inference-core composition required.
